1: A transformation is fixed only by its parameters: a reflection needs its mirror line, and a rotation needs its centre, angle and direction. Without them the image is not uniquely determined.
2: A column vector splits a movement into across and up parts. Because the parts are independent, vectors add and subtract component by component.
3: The magnitude is the length of the vector. Pythagoras on the two components gives that length.
4: Going from A to B is the same as going from the origin to B and back to A, so AB = b − a. The midpoint is halfway, so its position vector is the average of the two.
